note: All 185 bundles read (86 Middle Irish, 99 Middle Welsh pivots). No claim defended. Leads examined and rejected: BC-e5551 MIr snechta ... fri cnai n-olla ~ OHG Notker sne ... also wolla (snow likened to wool, cognate pair *sneygwh- + *h2wlh1neh2) is not inherited: the OHG is Notker's rendering of Psalm 147:16 nivem sicut lanam and the Irish is the Middle Irish Alexander history (Irische Texte II, from Latin sources, e.g. the Epistola Alexandri), so the simile is Latin/Biblical in both; the cognates are only basic vocabulary; BC-c82a2 Welsh poeth ... brych ~ RV/AV uksanam prsnim apacanta (*pekw- + *perk-) is chance, contexts unrelated (sickness description vs sacrifice); BC-9ed96 Welsh gas ... cudd ~ Beowulf hete ... hord (*keh2d- + *kewdh-) chance alliterative co-occurrence; BC-4c5f3 Welsh gnawt gwynt ~ Skt vayur ... na jnatah different syntax/sense; BC-57d96 Welsh derw/onn ~ Voluspa askr/tre no shared phrase; BC-4279e kinship lists generic. Most partners are late Greek prose and mappings of Celtic forms are frequently wrong (e.g. m-broin = bron sorrow, not bro quern).
